title: Jeremiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 15.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 15, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The LORD begins speaking to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 15:1.

questions.question: What did the LORD say would happen to those who are for death?
options: They will go forth to death
questions.correctAnswer: They will go forth to death
questions.explanation: The verse states that such as are for death, to death they shall go (Jeremiah 15:2).

questions.question: What four kinds did the LORD appoint over the people?
questions.explanation: The four kinds appointed over them are the sword, dogs, fowls, and beasts (Jeremiah 15:3).

questions.question: Who was mentioned as a reason for the people's removal into all kingdoms?
questions.explanation: Manasseh, the son of Hezekiah, is mentioned as the reason for their removal (Jeremiah 15:4).

questions.question: What question does the LORD ask about pity for Jerusalem?
options: Who shall have pity upon thee?
questions.correctAnswer: Who shall have pity upon thee?
questions.explanation: The verse asks who shall have pity upon Jerusalem (Jeremiah 15:5).

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the people's actions?
questions.explanation: The LORD states that they have forsaken Him (Jeremiah 15:6).

questions.question: What will the LORD do because He is weary with repenting?
options: He will stretch out His hand against them
questions.correctAnswer: He will stretch out His hand against them
questions.explanation: The LORD says He will stretch out His hand against them because He is weary with repenting (Jeremiah 15:6).

questions.question: What action does the LORD say He will take in the gates of the land?
questions.explanation: The LORD states He will bereave them of children in the gates of the land (Jeremiah 15:7).

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to His people?
options: They will return to their ways
questions.explanation: The LORD says He will destroy His people since they return not from their ways (Jeremiah 15:7).

questions.question: Did the LORD express a desire to have pity on the people?
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He could not have pity toward this people (Jeremiah 15:1).

questions.question: Is there a mention of children in Jeremiah 15?
questions.explanation: Children are mentioned when the LORD says He will bereave them of children (Jeremiah 15:7).

questions.question: Jeremiah 15 states that the LORD will cause destruction.
questions.explanation: The text states that the LORD will destroy His people (Jeremiah 15:7).

questions.question: The LORD mentioned Moses and Samuel as intercessors for the people.
questions.explanation: The LORD mentions Moses and Samuel standing before Him (Jeremiah 15:1).

questions.question: The LORD promises to restore Jerusalem in this chapter.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention any promise of restoration for Jerusalem (Jeremiah 15:1-7).

questions.question: The people of Jerusalem are described as righteous in this chapter.
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the people have forsaken the LORD and are going backward (Jeremiah 15:6).

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah compare the number of widows to?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:8 states, 'Their widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 15:9 indicate will happen to those who have borne children?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:9 mentions, 'She that hath borne seven languisheth.'

questions.question: What is Jeremiah's lament about his existence in Jeremiah 15:10?
options: He is a man of joy
He is a man of strife
He is a man of peace
He is a man of wealth
questions.correctAnswer: He is a man of strife
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:10 states, 'Woe is me, my mother, that thou hast borne me a man of strife.'

questions.question: What promise does the LORD give in Jeremiah 15:11 regarding the remnant?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:11 promises, 'Verily it shall be well with thy remnant.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 15:12 ask about iron?
options: Can iron break the northern iron and steel?
questions.correctAnswer: Can iron break the northern iron and steel?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:12 asks, 'Shall iron break the northern iron and the steel?'

questions.question: What will happen to Jeremiah's substance and treasures according to Jeremiah 15:13?
options: They will be given to the spoil
They will be taken by allies
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given to the spoil
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:13 states, 'Thy substance and thy treasures will I give to the spoil without price.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 15:14 say about the fate of the people?
options: They will return to their land
They will go to a land unknown
questions.correctAnswer: They will go to a land unknown
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:14 states, 'I will make thee to pass with thine enemies into a land which thou knowest not.'

questions.question: What consequence does Jeremiah 15:6 mention for forsaking the LORD?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:6 states, 'therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 15:5, who is said to have pity upon Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:5 asks, 'For who shall have pity upon thee, O Jerusalem?'.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 15:3 list as one of the appointed kinds of destruction?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:3 mentions, 'the sword to slay.'

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I am weary with repenting' in Jeremiah 15:6 imply about God's feelings?
questions.explanation: This is correct because the phrase suggests God's frustration with the people's unrepentance as stated in Jeremiah 15:6.

questions.question: The remnant will be treated well in times of evil according to which verse?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:11 states that the enemy will entreat the remnant well in times of affliction.

questions.question: Jeremiah expresses a sense of contention in his life. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Jeremiah states in Jeremiah 15:10, 'I have borne a man of strife and contention.'

questions.question: Jeremiah believes he has lent on usury according to Jeremiah 15:10. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah states, 'I have neither lent on usury,' indicating he has not done so.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 15:14, the people will prosper in a new land. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Jeremiah 15:14 indicates they will be taken into a land unknown, implying suffering and punishment.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 15.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 15:15, what does Jeremiah ask the LORD to do for him?
options: Remember me, visit me, and revenge me of my persecutors
Destroy my enemies and give me wealth
Grant me peace and long life
Send me to a foreign land
questions.correctAnswer: Remember me, visit me, and revenge me of my persecutors
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:15 states, 'remember me, and visit me, and revenge me of my persecutors.' This is his direct request to the LORD.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 15:16, what effect did God's words have on Jeremiah?
options: They were the joy and rejoicing of his heart
They made him fearful and anxious
questions.correctAnswer: They were the joy and rejoicing of his heart
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:16 says, 'thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart,' showing the positive impact of God's words.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 15:17, why does Jeremiah say he sat alone?
options: Because of God's hand filling him with indignation
questions.correctAnswer: Because of God's hand filling him with indignation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:17 states, 'I sat alone because of thy hand: for thou hast filled me with indignation,' explaining the cause of his solitude.

questions.question: What complaint does Jeremiah make about his suffering in Jeremiah 15:18?
options: His pain is perpetual and his wound incurable
questions.correctAnswer: His pain is perpetual and his wound incurable
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:18 says, 'Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable,' highlighting his ongoing anguish.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 15:19, what condition does the LORD give for Jeremiah to stand before Him?
options: If Jeremiah returns and takes forth the precious from the vile
If Jeremiah flees to another land
questions.correctAnswer: If Jeremiah returns and takes forth the precious from the vile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:19 states, 'If thou return, then will I bring thee again... and if thou take forth the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth.'

questions.question: What promise does the LORD make to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 15:20 regarding his protection?
options: He will make him a fenced brasen wall and he shall not be prevailed against
He will make him king over Israel
He will hide him from all enemies
He will grant him riches and honor
questions.correctAnswer: He will make him a fenced brasen wall and he shall not be prevailed against
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:20 says, 'I will make thee unto this people a fenced brasen wall... they shall not prevail against thee,' promising divine protection.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'tsadaq' in Jeremiah 15:15 most closely mean?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 15:15, the word translated as 'remember' comes from the Hebrew root 'zakar' rather than 'tsadaq'; however, focusing on 'remember' reveals the meaning 'to remember, recall,' which is the correct semantic range here.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Jeremiah 15:16 where Jeremiah says, 'Thy words were found, and I did eat them'?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:16 uses metaphor by describing God's words as food to be eaten, symbolizing internalization and acceptance.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Jeremiah 15:15's theme of suffering for God's sake and pleading for deliverance?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 3:12 states, 'Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution,' echoing Jeremiah 15:15's theme of suffering for God's sake.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage most closely connects with Jeremiah 15:20 about God making a 'fenced brasen wall' to protect His servant?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 41:10 promises God's presence and strength to protect His people, paralleling Jeremiah 15:20's promise of protection as a 'fenced brasen wall.'

questions.question: What immediately precedes Jeremiah's plea in Jeremiah 15:15?
options: A pronouncement of judgment and exile upon the people
A prophecy of restoration and peace
A vision of the new covenant
An exhortation to build an altar
questions.correctAnswer: A pronouncement of judgment and exile upon the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:1-14 describes judgment, exile, and destruction due to sin, immediately preceding Jeremiah 15:15's personal plea.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 15:18, Jeremiah asks if God will be 'as waters that fail.' What literary device is this an example of?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:18 uses 'as waters that fail' as a simile comparing God's faithfulness to unstable water.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah describe his social interactions in Jeremiah 15:17?
options: He did not sit with mockers and sat alone
questions.correctAnswer: He did not sit with mockers and sat alone
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:17 says, 'I sat not in the assembly of the mockers... I sat alone,' describing his isolation.

questions.question: Which theme is strongly foreshadowed in Jeremiah 15:21 where God promises to deliver and redeem Jeremiah out of the hand of the wicked and terrible?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:21's promise of deliverance and redemption typologically foreshadows the ultimate deliverance through Jesus Christ (cf. Luke 4:18).

questions.question: Jeremiah 15:19 mentions being 'as my mouth' if he takes forth the precious from the vile. What is the significance of this metaphor?
options: It implies Jeremiah will be God's spokesperson
It means Jeremiah will become wealthy
It suggests Jeremiah will become a judge
It indicates Jeremiah will be a warrior
questions.correctAnswer: It implies Jeremiah will be God's spokesperson
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:19's phrase 'thou shalt be as my mouth' signifies Jeremiah acting as God's prophet and spokesperson to the people.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 15:1 teach about God's disposition toward sinful humanity?
options: God's judgment is irrevocable despite intercession
God is always willing to forgive upon repentance
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is irrevocable despite intercession
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:1 shows that even if great intercessors like Moses and Samuel stood before God, His mind would not be toward the people, indicating His judgment stands despite intercession.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is taught in Jeremiah 15:3?
options: God appoints diverse instruments to execute judgment
God punishes only the guilty leaders
God delays judgment for a long time
God limits judgment to a single form of punishment
questions.correctAnswer: God appoints diverse instruments to execute judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:3 teaches that God will use multiple agents—sword, dogs, birds, and beasts—to bring destruction, showing the multifaceted nature of divine justice.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine discipline and human responsibility is taught in Jeremiah 15:6?
options: God is weary of repentance when people refuse to turn
God will discipline but never destroy His people
Human sin does not affect God's actions
God's wrath is arbitrary and unprovoked
questions.correctAnswer: God is weary of repentance when people refuse to turn
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:6 reveals God's weariness with repenting because the people have forsaken Him and gone backward, highlighting human responsibility in divine discipline.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 15:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:11 promises well-being for the remnant and divine intervention in their affliction, demonstrating God's faithfulness to His covenant people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 15:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:20 portrays God making Jeremiah a 'fenced brasen wall' and assuring his deliverance, highlighting God's protective nature toward His servants.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 15:4 connect to the broader biblical theme of exile as punishment for covenant unfaithfulness?
options: It predicts the scattering of Israel due to Manasseh's sins
It denies any punishment for kings' sins
It emphasizes exile as a blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It predicts the scattering of Israel due to Manasseh's sins
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:4 explicitly links exile ('removed into all kingdoms') to Manasseh's sins, reflecting the biblical theme that covenant unfaithfulness leads to scattering.

questions.question: In what way does Jeremiah 15:16 prepare for the New Testament understanding of the Word of God as sustenance and joy?
options: It depicts God's word as nourishment and rejoicing in the prophet's heart
It describes the word as a burden and sorrow
It denies the importance of God's word
It shows God's word as irrelevant to human life
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts God's word as nourishment and rejoicing in the prophet's heart
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:16 uses the metaphor of eating God's words as joy and rejoicing, prefiguring New Testament themes where the Word sustains and enlivens believers.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 15:6 and Jeremiah 15:7 teach about God's response to persistent sin?
options: God's judgment intensifies when people refuse repentance
God quickly forgives all sins without consequence
God ignores persistent sin to show mercy
God's wrath is limited to natural disasters
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment intensifies when people refuse repentance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:6 speaks of God's weariness with repenting and judgment; 15:7 describes further destruction because of unrepentance, showing intensification of judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 15:10 and Jeremiah 15:15 teach about the prophet's experience in relation to divine calling?
options: Prophets suffer rejection and rely on God for vindication
Prophets are always honored and applauded
Prophetic ministry is free from personal hardship
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets suffer rejection and rely on God for vindication
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:10 shows Jeremiah's lament about being cursed despite innocence, and 15:15 is a plea for God to remember and avenge him, illustrating prophetic suffering and reliance on God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 15:19 and Jeremiah 15:20 teach about divine restoration and protection for the faithful?
options: Return to God results in restoration and divine safeguarding
Restoration is unconditional regardless of behavior
Faithfulness leads to human protection only
Divine protection excludes the possibility of suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Return to God results in restoration and divine safeguarding
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:19 promises restoration if the prophet returns, and 15:20 assures God will protect him like a brass wall, combining restoration and protection themes.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 15:1-3 shows God as unjust and arbitrary in judgment. What does Jeremiah 15:1-3 actually teach?
options: God's judgment is righteous and sovereign, even beyond intercession
God punishes without cause or pattern
God is indifferent and disconnected from human affairs
God's judgment is based on random chance
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is righteous and sovereign, even beyond intercession
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:1-3 demonstrates that even great intercessors cannot alter God's just judgment, underscoring His righteous sovereignty, not arbitrariness.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine wrath and covenant judgment is taught in Jeremiah 15:13?
options: God's wrath leads to loss of wealth as punishment for sin
God's wrath spares the treasures of the faithful
God's judgment is limited to spiritual consequences only
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath leads to loss of wealth as punishment for sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:13 declares God will give treasures to spoil because of sins, illustrating covenant judgment affecting material possessions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Jeremiah 15:14's description of God's anger?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:14 speaks of a fire kindled in God's anger burning upon the people, reflecting God's holy intolerance of sin.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 15:9 contribute to the biblical understanding of communal suffering due to sin?
options: It portrays the widespread grief and shame affecting families
It minimizes the effects of sin on the community
It suggests only individuals suffer consequences
It describes sin as a private matter
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the widespread grief and shame affecting families
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:9 vividly describes mothers mourning and shame, revealing communal suffering as a result of sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 15:17 and Jeremiah 15:18 teach about the prophet's emotional struggle and faith?
options: Prophetic suffering involves anguish and questioning God's faithfulness
Prophets always experience peace and clarity
Faith negates any experience of doubt
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic suffering involves anguish and questioning God's faithfulness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 15:17 shows Jeremiah sitting alone in indignation, and 15:18 questions the perpetuity of pain and God's reliability, reflecting emotional struggle.
